# CLAIMs with `line` `nucleating-argument`

*Lines of inquiry — A named line of the record's own argument, so that a line can be set aside as a whole and what depends on it can be found. Retracting a line is a status change on its members, never a deletion (ADR-032).*

**Nucleating an argument** — how an argument developed across stateless sessions settles into stable, addressable structure — what drifts, what anchors it, and what anchoring costs. What a record of it keeps, and the record as its own apparatus, are lines of their own (ADR-082).

| [CLAIM-785](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-785.md) | Adding a predicate to an entry is adding a constraint on its revisions: each field filled, relation drawn, status set, defeater stated and passage quoted is a test its later versions must pass, so as they accrue the revisions still open to it are an intersection that only shrinks, toward what the predicates say, which its filers chose; the inductive prior an entry develops is that intersection weighted by how hard each predicate is enforced, from prose convention to lint rule; accruing predicates stabilizes an entry, in the control-theoretic sense, in the dimensions they constrain, and narrowing it is not good in itself | The owner's reframe, 2026-11-21: "maybe it works better if I say 'stabilization' instead of 'contraction'. my suggestion here is a reframe of how adding predicates to an item is a manifestation of adding constraints", with the pointer that the record maps predicates to test functions. | [CLAIM-789](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-789.md) v2 | In any inquiry whose sources are revised, copying exactly anchors a copy to the version it was taken from, so the copy keeps what a later revision removed: exact copying conserves staleness as faithfully as content, and what anchors a derived text to a revisable source is a tie to the source that a revision has to pass through, not exactness | [CLAIM-772](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-772.md) makes exact copying the record's means of anchoring content. | [CLAIM-793](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-793.md) v2 | Where an inquiry keeps its sources and each step reads the stored source rather than the last restatement of it, re-reading is not a second route beside conservation but conservation on the state enlarged by the source; on that structure an interpretation does not drift but settles on a fixed offset from the source toward the reader's prior, the same at every reading, which no reader sharing that prior can see, and drift is confined to the chains of derived texts | [CLAIM-772](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-772.md) models anchoring as a chain whose steps copy the source's features exactly, and sets aside Friedkin and Johnsen's re-injection of the start as a second route it does not cover.
